quests.storyParagraph: Many first-time bakers give up on sourdough after one flat loaf. The problem is usually not their technique but their starter. A starter needs about a week of regular feeding before it is strong enough to raise dough. Bakers who skip this stage often see little or no rise. By contrast, those who wait for bubbles and a sour smell tend to get an open, airy crumb. Patience at the start therefore matters more than skill later.

quests.storyParagraph: Psychologists have long noticed that people remember unfinished tasks better than finished ones. This is sometimes called the Zeigarnik effect, after the researcher who described it. She observed waiters recalling open orders in detail but forgetting paid ones. The explanation is that an unfinished task keeps a kind of mental tension alive until it is resolved. Once the task ends, the tension fades, and so does the memory. Students can use this by stopping a study session in the middle of a problem. The unfinished problem will stay in mind and make it easier to resume.

quests.storyParagraph: Bees find flowers with remarkable accuracy. When a scout discovers a rich patch, she returns to the hive and performs a waggle dance. It is one of the few known examples of symbolic communication in insects.
